citations.review_text: I don’t know what it is, but this game sucks ballz. I have no issue with PvPvPvPvPvPvPvPvEvT or any of the sweaty stinklord dorks who play that… although I prefer PvEvEvEvEvEvE. It’s the content that rubs my buns wrong. Feels like a worse version of every other extraction shooter mixed with tons of flossing, adolescent and unstable Fartnight cringe.

I was excited for ARC Raiders when it was presented as a PvE experience, but removing that mode completely killed my interest. 
Not everyone wants to spend their time dealing with PvP players, rats hiding in corners, griefers, and people whose only goal is to ruin someone else's match.

I enjoy cooperative gameplay where players work together against the game's challenges, not constant paranoia about getting ambushed by someone camping an extraction point. 
The shift to an extraction PvPvE format feels like the game abandoned the audience that was originally interested in it.

It's disappointing to see a unique PvE concept replaced with yet another PvP-focused experience. 
For players like me, this change turned a must-play game into an easy pass.

claims.claim: Reviewers report encountering difficulties and errors when trying to link accounts or manage cross-progression.

citations.review_text:
Originally got the game on PlayStation, bought it again on sale when all the recent Sony BS started happening. After 2 straight weeks of trying to link accounts to migrate over from PSN to Steam, the site refusing to link Steam specifically unless I created an entirely new account which would then refuse to link PSN but both times, would link everything from Discord to XBOX when I don't even own an XBOX or this game on XBOX.
And after joining the Discord to try and contact a singular human Customer Service Agent after dealing with their awful AI chat bot, I finally get a hold of someone and upon explaining my situation and all I wanted was to link accounts, which is a service they blatantly advertise both on their website and in game. I got perma-banned with no warning or reason, so despite owning the game for over 2+ weeks, I got a refund, thank you Steam and Embark can go fuck themselves. I actually liked your game, I was excited for pure PvE and I I'm not even allowed to play it.

Horrible account system ruins a great game

I really want to play this game, but the account system created by Embark is an absolute nightmare.
When you first launch the game on PC via the Xbox App, the game automatically creates a "ghost" Embark ID in the background and locks your Xbox account to it immediately—without asking or giving you a choice. If you already have a main profile (like from PS5) and want to link your Xbox account to use cross-progression, you are completely locked out. The website just gives you a useless error saying "the account has content saved", even if you have 0 minutes of playtime on PC.
There is NO logout button in the game. You have to contact the support via text tickets and wait for hours or days just to get a simple empty account unlinked. And even AFTER the support finally unlinks it, the system hits you with a hidden, hardcoded 24-hour lockout timer before you can reconnect it to your real profile.
It is incredibly frustrating that honest players who actually bought the game are blocked from playing for days because of poorly designed, over-complicated security measures. Fix your login system, Embark. This is completely unacceptable.

citations.review_text: cool atmosphere. plays well even on i5 3rd gen with a 1060 3gb. ill buy soon.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ **5/5 Stars**

ARC Raiders is honestly an amazing game. The graphics are great, the gameplay is fun, and every match feels like a new experience. The PvE and PvP elements make every encounter exciting, and the extraction mechanics keep you on your toes. Exploring the world, fighting ARC machines, collecting loot, and escaping with your gear makes the game incredibly satisfying.

Whether you're playing solo or with friends, there's always something exciting happening. Definitely worth playing if you enjoy extraction shooters. I can't wait to see what the developers add next!

**10/10 would recommend!**

[h1] Anthropocentrism [/h1]

I bought this game because I thought PVE was going to be a permanent solution to a [strike]problem[/strike] "feature" that I foresaw when the game first launched. Back then, I knew I wouldn't like it because of the type of players it attracts. When I saw that the game now had a dedicated PVE mode, I bought it thinking I could finally experience the game for its art and world.

But it turns out that PVE is [b]not[/b] the solution, because it doesn't fix something you can't fix: the toxicity of the player base.

I haven't survived a single round of PVP, and I've never been saved by another player when I've been downed.

It's just not my cup of tea, but that's not why I don't recommend it.

This game has such a cool art direction, great optimization (when it works), and an atmosphere like no other game. The ARC enemies are fun to fight, and the sound design is probably the best I've ever heard in a video game. The sound designers really, really cooked here!!

The reason I can't recommend this game is the nature of the gameplay model itself.

The players are rough, loud, and annoying, and they find creative ways to mess with you—even in PVE mode. They'll wait until you die to loot your corpse instead of helping you. If you're in a pinch and get the chance to request a supply drop, they'll crawl out of every crevice on the map like moths to a flame—and steal it right in front of you. They'll stand in your way, make loud noises around new players to attract ARC for no reason, and close the extraction point right in front of you. They'll strip the map of valuable loot before you've even figured out where to look for it.

Half the time, the loot feels meaningless anyway, yet the game makes sure you'll have to go to YouTube just to figure out what to keep, recycle, or sell. Your inventory is always full, and expanding it gets progressively more expensive, meaning you'll eventually have to get rid of things you originally wanted to…

Its a very enjoyable fun game. I liked the combat and the enviroment looks amazing! Loved it.

So why am I not recommending it? Because I bought it specifically for the PvE mode. I bought it knowing it was only for a week and I was okay with it. And coming from a PvE perspective - I cant recommend it simply because...there is no more PvE. 

As much as I enjoyed playing through that week - I wont be coming back until PvE is permament. And all the same - this review wont be positive until said PvE mode will be permament. 

Few things from the PvE test to improve before it returns permamently:

1. Turn off player collision completely.
2. Make it possible for players to lock down the loot room from others. Its dumb to use a card when someone already went through it.
3. Allow us to revive other players without needing the stimpack(or whatever its called in english)

Also appearently there are some griefers in PvE mode? I personally havent encountered any but Ive seen many posts online about some toxicity.

I really wanted to like ARC Raiders, especially because the graphics look fantastic, but I just couldn't get into it. The gameplay got repetitive pretty quickly, and I found myself getting more frustrated than actually having fun.

I got tired of constantly going out to collect loot, only to risk losing everything because of another player. I know that's part of an extraction shooter, but it doesn't make it any less annoying. Sometimes I just wanted to explore or complete objectives without having to worry about someone coming along and ruining all that progress.

The progression also felt like a grind, and after a while, doing the same things over and over became exhausting. I don't mind challenging games, but I want to feel like my time is being rewarded, not wasted.

It's a shame because the game looks great and has an interesting concept. I can understand why some people enjoy it, but personally, I found it more frustrating than fun. Definitely not worth the hype for me.

ARC Raiders is an incredibly refreshing take on the extraction shooter genre. The combination of exploration, survival, intense encounters, and cooperative gameplay creates an experience that keeps you coming back for more.

The world is beautifully designed, the atmosphere is immersive, and the gameplay rewards both strategy and teamwork. Whether you're exploring the surface, collecting valuable resources, or encountering other players, there's always something interesting happening.

Overall, ARC Raiders is a fantastic experience for anyone looking for something different in the multiplayer shooter genre. Highly recommended! I love interacting with my fellow gamers here always some stories to share after an long day.

One of the Best Games I've Ever Bought

ARC Raiders is genuinely one of the best games I've ever purchased. It has an incredibly immersive atmosphere that makes you pay attention to every little detail in the environment, whether you're looking for cover, searching for loot, or simply trying to stay alive.

Even though the maps aren't enormous, the variety of locations, atmospheres, and activities makes each raid feel like a different experience.

### Simple Gameplay, Deep Tactical Experience

ARC Raiders has one of the simplest yet most tactical gameplay loops in its genre. The shooting mechanics are straightforward: aim and shoot. However, the variety of guns and weapons keeps combat exciting, whether you're fighting other players or taking on ARC enemies.

### An Incredible Atmosphere

The detailed environments, dynamic world, and precise sound design take the experience to another level. Sound isn't just there for immersion; it also plays an important tactical role, adding tension, excitement, and a constant sense of uncertainty.

The game is also exceptionally well optimized. I've experienced no graphical or performance issues, and I can maintain around 100–150 FPS at maximum graphics settings on my PC. That's more than enough for my 75Hz monitor.

### The Perfect Balance Between PvE and PvP

One of the things I appreciate most is the balance between PvE and PvP. There aren't so many players that quests become constantly frustrating, but the world doesn't feel empty either.

Player interactions are unpredictable. Sometimes people are friendly and willing to cooperate; other times, they'll attack you without hesitation. You can never fully trust anyone, and that uncertainty creates a genuine post-apocalyptic survival experience.

### Plenty of Reasons to Keep Playing

Million-dollar concept completely butchered by brain-dead live-service management. A masterclass in how to kill a game with massive potential.
Let’s be honest: ARC Raiders has a phenomenal foundation. The Rust Belt setting, the gorgeous Unreal Engine 5 visuals, the snappy movement, and the sheer satisfaction of blowing apart metallic killer robots could have easily flipped the entire extraction shooter genre on its head. It could have been the next decade-defining multiplayer game. Instead, Embark Studios is running it like a complete joke. It honestly feels like this multi-million dollar project is being held hostage by a skeleton crew of three clueless developers who have absolutely no idea how a live-service loop is supposed to function.
After pouring hours into this game, the honeymoon phase is completely dead, and the ugly reality sets in. This game is an empty, mind-numbing chore that completely fails to respect your time.
Here is a detailed breakdown of why this game is aggressively boring and rapidly bleeding its player base:
1. A completely dead economy and an insulting loot pool
The primary driving force behind any great extraction shooter is the dopamine hit of finding good loot. In this game, 90% of the world is cluttered with low-tier "white" and "green" garbage that becomes completely useless after your first weekend. There is absolutely no reason to pick most of it up. Why is the loot pool so shallow? Look at games like Terraria—they have thousands of unique items, rare drops, and accessories that make every single run feel like a slot machine jackpot. ARC Raiders doesn't have that. It doesn't even have a basic scrap/recycling mechanic. Why can't I dismantle this endless mountain of useless junk in my workshop to accumulate raw materials for high-tier crafting? Once you get your baseline gear, you stop looting entirely. You are just running through a ghost town looking for the 2 or 3 specific items that actually matter. The economy is fundamentally br…

I have over 300 hours on this account and atleast 150 hours on a second account, and I gotta say this game is fucking amazing from the general Gameplay loop, to the world itself, the enemy design, sound design, I LOVE this game. but, ever since the PvE week where the mode was tested.....I never want to go back, ever again, the devs said they tried this game as just a PvE game and they found it boring....but I as well as many others love every other aspect other than the PvP infact the PvP takes away from enjoying the other aspects of the game.  I will still continue to play every now and again, but the desire to grind up the cool new stuff only for it be snagged away by a group of people hiding around a corner, stripping away hours of grinding. I would rather lose it to an insane Arc Bossfight or event, because atleast that was within my control. I will happily change my review to a positive one once there is a Permanent PvE mode introduced

well worth the money, fun play through with lots of repeatability, new content at a quarterly pace allows this team to do what they do best and deliver quality over 'new shiny' that a lot of games fall into.  one of the most impressive things with this game is the sound quality and realism.

citations.review_text:
If you are looking for a game to play with a full trio in PVE i would highly advise against Arc Raiders until Embark is done with the dedicated PVE mode. You will get nothing done if you are trying to farm items, complete quests. Or fight ARCs. You can have raids where people prepare dedicated ambush kits and just sit there farming people who come by, or roam the map on a warpath for no reason other than to PVP and steal your shit. Keep in mind this game is primarily marketed AND updated as a PVE experience.
Solo or duo riads are generally highly enjoyable. But as an overall multiplayer experience? I've havent seen many games as toxic as this. Especially with how cancerous farming for components or niche items is. Let alone acquiring any decent gear.

This doesen't include the heaps of bugs that are also present. Quests unable to be completed due to broken interactions, ARCs being able to see and/or hit you through walls or invisible gaps. Among other things.

10/10 – This game has given me trust issues.

I went into ARC Raiders thinking I'd be fighting robots and collecting loot.

Instead, I've learned that the most dangerous thing in this game is a grown man saying "friendly, friendly" over proximity chat.

I've been shot in the back, robbed of everything I own, and emotionally manipulated by someone who sounded like he had a mortgage and three kids.

I'll spend 25 minutes carefully looting, avoiding every possible threat, just to get absolutely folded by a guy named "xXBootySnatcherXx" camping extraction.

Every time I die, I tell myself I'm getting off.

Every time I get off, I'm back on 10 minutes later.

I have nothing in my stash, no faith in humanity, and a concerning amount of hours played.

10/10. My therapist says I need to learn how to trust people again. I told her "friendly, friendly" and stole her wallet.

Also to add, Embark puts more effort into banning casual Dad gamers that kill streamers: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OI7UAPs9sLU
